names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 6 aprilie, «Sfântul Cuvios Grigorie Sinaitul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 11 Φεβρουαρίου, «Όσιος Γρηγόριος ο Σιναΐτης», with the rank word left off.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 6 Απριλίου, «Όσιος Γρηγόριος ο Σιναΐτης», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's fifth heading for the Julian 7 April on pravoslavno.rs, „Преп. Григорије Синаит.“, with the rank word Преп. left off. The by-name Синаит is kept: it is what the heading gives beyond the forename, and `gregory-of-nyssa` and `gregory-of-moesia` already hold the bare Григорије, which a bare form here would fold onto.

birth.note: saint.gr's heading for him on the 11 Φεβρουαρίου page, «Οσιος Γρηγοριος ο Σιναϊτης (1255 - 1347)». doxologia.ro, cited on this folder's Romanian row, gave no year of birth.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «sfântul Grigorie a trecut la Domnul pe 27 noiembrie 1346 și este prăznuit pe 6 aprilie.» saint.gr's heading on its 11 Φεβρουαρίου page gives «(1255 - 1347)» and argues for neither year; the attested day and year are kept and the disagreement is recorded rather than averaged into an interval.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (19 September 2026).

feast.note: The life page says he died on 27 November 1346 and is kept on 6 April: «Sfântul Grigorie a trecut la Domnul pe 27 noiembrie 1346 și este prăznuit pe 6 aprilie.» The day of death and the day of commemoration are different, and 6 aprilie is the day the calendar prints him on.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 6 aprilie — «Sfântul Cuvios Grigorie Sinaitul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 11ης Φεβρουαρίου — «Όσιος Γρηγόριος ο Σιναΐτης»

attestations.note: The page saint.gr serves on this day is a stub: it heads him «Οσιος Γρηγοριος ο Σιναϊτης (1255 - 1347)», declares the feast fixed on 11 Φεβρουαρίου, and for the life sends the reader elsewhere — «Βλέπε βιογραφικό του σημείωμα στις 6 Απριλίου». 6 April is the day this folder's Romanian row already keeps him on, off doxologia.ro. This row records the Greek day page read; whether saint.gr's 6 April is a second Greek commemoration or only where it files the life has not been established here, and no second row is made for it. saint.gr keeps him a second time on 6 Απριλίου, «Όσιος Γρηγόριος ο Σιναΐτης», which is the day doxologia gives for him as well; one attestation row per church is the schema, so the 11 Φεβρουαρίου row read first is kept and the April day is recorded here.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.04.2026 (7. април ст. ст.) — „Преп. Григорије Синаит.“

attestations.note: The day's fifth and shortest entry, and **it is a cross-reference**: the whole of it is „Велики светитељ и подвижник Синајски и Атонски. (Види 8. август).“ — a great saint and ascetic of Sinai and of Athos, see 8 August. The identity is beyond doubt and nothing is added: no year, no place beyond Sinai and Athos, no fact this folder does not already carry from doxologia.ro and saint.gr. **The row carries the day that was read, 7 April, because this folder had no Serbian row at all and this is the first; the Julian 8 August is where the Prologue prints the account, and the reader who reaches that day must add `BRIEF.md` §4's second-day note rather than move this row.** That is named in the run's findings, with the reason: the first Serbian day read wins the row by the settled rule, and the order of reading is what decides it. The folder now carries three days on three calendars — the Romanian 6 April, the Greek 11 February and the Serbian 7 April — and a fourth owed as a note; all of them are the sources' own and none was computed. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion, and this folder has no hymn from any source.
